overall_summary: Analysis of 46 deduplicated uploads shows a stark performance divergence: immersive space 'What If' survival hooks and extreme planetary anomalies consistently generate the highest traction (400–1,050+ views, 3–4.6% like rates, active comments), whereas repetitive psychology facts, duplicate re-uploads, and low-stakes biological trivia stagnate under 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Planetary Survival Hooks ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) outperformed channel averages by 4x to 8x.
winning_patterns.action: Use visceral second-person sensory immersion ('What if you stepped onto...') targeting exotic, high-hazard celestial bodies.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Space Superlatives & Dark Cosmic Anomalies
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views, 25 likes) drove strong like ratios (3.4–3.5%) and comment engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor titles on singular, mind-bending scientific superlatives paired with cinematic visualization of extreme environments.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple variations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined at 5, 10, and 53 views; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' reached only 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause generic psychology tips unless framed as a high-stakes psychological micro-thriller or biological survival mystery.

weak_patterns.pattern: Direct Duplicate Re-uploads Without Creative Evolution
weak_patterns.evidence: Re-posting identical titles like 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' (views dropped from 220 to 87 and 34) and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' yields diminishing algorithm distribution.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict anti-repetition; iterate on winning pacing and hooks rather than recycling previously published topics.
